Limited test drives. My family was in the market to purchase a truck and found at least 4 here that we wanted to test drive with the intention to buy same day. It’s hard getting the family together and off work on the same day but we made it out. After test driving the second truck we were told we could only look at one more. We chose to forgo looking any more and the owners seemed quite happy about and content to lose a sale.  We were talking on the way back from our last test drive about buying the first one we drove, but wanted to make sure. There were three of the same make and model as well as three others of a different make and model. This unfortunate event is compounded by the fact that we drove an hour away but thought it was worth the drive as there were several trucks we were interested in and the online reviews looked good. Lesson learned.

PS I’m positive that all the good reviews on here are BOTs. The quality of cars they have pictured  do not check with what we saw in person. In addition the reviews mention excellent customer service and unwavering patience 🤣 we were run off for being to interested
*****Update!!!*****
And the response from the owners validate the points that I made. We were looking for a truck and trying to decide between two make/models. It’s unreasonable to pick one of the three Toyotas and one of the three Nissans to be able to test drive and expect the other four to drive the same.

So glad that we missed out on getting a truck from this place, I looked at all the one star reviews and 🔥🔥🔥🔥🔥🔥

I wouldn’t recommend this dealership to anyone who actually wants to compare vehicles before making a purchase.

My family and I came here fully intending to buy a truck the same day. We drove an hour because they had several vehicles we were interested in — multiple trucks of the same make/model along with a few comparable options from another brand. Since every used vehicle drives differently, we wanted to narrow down the best one by test driving a few of them. That’s a normal part of shopping for a vehicle.

After only two test drives, we were told we could only drive one more vehicle. That immediately killed the entire buying experience. We weren’t joyriding or wasting anyone’s time — we were serious buyers trying to make an informed decision on a major purchase.

What made the situation even more frustrating was the mixed messaging. As we were leaving, they repeatedly asked if we wanted to test drive another vehicle, while at the same time acting irritated that we wanted to compare options in the first place. If there’s a strict limit on what customers are “allowed” to test drive before spending thousands of dollars, that should be stated upfront.

The owner’s response to other reviews only reinforces the issue. Expecting customers to drive one Toyota and one Nissan and assume the other trucks on the lot will feel identical is unrealistic, especially with used vehicles where condition, maintenance, mileage, tires, suspension, and wear can make a huge difference.

The online reviews and the experience we had in person did not match at all. We expected professionalism and patience from a dealership trying to earn a sale. Instead, we left feeling rushed and unwelcome despite being ready to buy.

Would not return.

DO NOT BUY FROM HERE. I bought a 2015 Hyundai Sonata in Feb 2026, and it didn't even last a month. By March, I was getting two oil changes in 30 days because of a major leak. When the engine light started flashing, the codes for the camshaft and knock sensor showed up as ‘stored,’ meaning the dealership likely cleared the lights to hide the issues from me. I paid to replace the knock sensor myself, but the engine light stayed on and the engine is now failing. When I went back for help, the salesman was basically telling my boyfriend that they already had our money and since it was ‘as-is,’ they didn't care. He tried to send us to a mechanic next door who just happened to be ‘leaving’ the second we pulled up. They had a Carfax in the window, but after doing my own digging, things are not adding up. They clearly patched up a dying engine with a temporary fix just to get it off the lot. Absolutely ridiculous and dishonest business. BTW Hyundai stated my engine is failing tremendously. I’m fine with the car being as is but when things are not adding up and things that are major that are happening too soon I’m already knowing something ain’t right like getting the tires rotated or getting the tires changed or getting a tuneup that’s understandable but the engine failing and two codes that has something to do with the engine is very weird. Lesson learn
